About the Role

Owns datacenter design and technical standards for Lambda’s AI infrastructure. Sets the basis of design, builds a repeatable and scalable set of reference designs, and leads the design team that delivers efficient, reliable, buildable facilities for current and next-generation GPU platforms.


What You’ll Do

Basis of design and standards

AI infrastructure readiness

Site master planning and design delivery

 - Drive prefabrication and modular delivery with Construction and the supply chain.

Equipment specification

 - Own owner-furnished equipment specifications and required equipment lists; review and approve vendor proposals and submittals.

 - Support long-lead equipment forecasting with Construction and procurement.

Team and quality

 - Lead the Mechanical Engineer, Electrical Engineer, Architect, and TPM; set design review and quality processes and hire as the portfolio grows.

 - Ensure code compliance and professional engineering oversight of design deliverables.

You

 - 15+ years designing critical facilities or datacenters, including 5+ years leading design teams.

 - Hands-on depth in mechanical (chilled water, heat rejection, liquid cooling) and electrical design for large-scale datacenters.

 - Experience developing design standards and reference designs for multi-site programs.

 - Experience managing third-party architecture and engineering firms and design budgets.

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or electrical engineering, or architecture; licensed Professional Engineer strongly preferred.

We are looking for a Senior Core Technology Engineer to design, build, and operate cloud-native microservices and large-scale data platforms for regulatory risk, credit calculation, and RWA aggregation and reporting under Optima.
You will work in a forward-deployed style . You will sit close to Risk, Finance, and Product users, turn their problems into working software, and own delivery through production. You will also use AI coding agents to raise team productivity while keeping quality, security, and auditability high.

What You'll Do
- Lead the design and delivery of fault-tolerant microservices and APIs on Spring Boot 4 and Java 21 / 25, deployed on OpenShift / Kubernetes.
- Own architecture for batch and streaming risk pipelines using Flink and Spark. Orchestrate them with Apache Airflow .
- Design the analytics layer. Serve low-latency risk and RWA analytics through Apache Pinot and expose them to users through Apache Superset dashboards.
- Design event-driven integrations across Kafka, RabbitMQ, and TIBCO. Architect data access and caching across Sybase, Oracle, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and Ignite / GridGain.
- Work directly with Risk and Finance stakeholders. Frame problems, prototype quickly, ship iteratively, and gather feedback from real users.
- Build and review software using AI coding agents (such as Devin and Claude) . Define team guardrails: approved tools, prompt and context hygiene, mandatory human review, and test-backed acceptance of agent-generated code.
- Set engineering standards across BDD testing, SonarQube gates, DevSecOps, and CVE remediation. Lead modernization (Java upgrades, Maven to Gradle, Ksh / Bash to Airflow).
- Lead design and code reviews, mentor C12 and junior engineers, and serve as an on-call escalation point.
Required Qualifications
- 8+ years of software engineering experience. Strong Java (17 required; 21 / 25 preferred), distributed systems, concurrency, and SQL.
- Deep Spring Boot experience (Batch, Integration, Security / OAuth2, Data, Kafka). Proven microservices and REST API design in production.
- Hands-on Flink and / or Spark , and production experience with Kafka plus one other messaging platform.

Amperos is healthcare's first AI-native denial management and revenue recovery platform. We just closed a $16M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with continued participation from Uncork Capital and Neo. We're reimagining enterprise Identity and Access Management from the ground up. Founded by serial entrepreneurs Shai Morag and Tal Marom and backed by a $60M seed round from Greylock, Accel, and CRV, we're building the next generation of identity security. Identity is the gateway to everything- who's let in, who's kept out, and it's now the number one attack vector in the enterprise. The tools built to govern it were designed for a slower world of human users and static environments. That world is gone. Identities are exploding across human, machine, and AI agents faster than legacy systems can track, and security teams are left patching together five disconnected tools that still can't answer "who has access to what, right now." We think the answer isn't another point solution- it's a new foundation. Oak is the AI-native Identity Operating System: an AI connector framework that reaches any application, a live identity graph built from raw evidence, and a team of AI agents that governs the full lifecycle of every identity in one platform. We're building Oak's AI-native core from day one-engineered for what enterprise identity is becoming, not patched onto what it used to be. And we're just getting started.

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix
Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe?
Pratt & Whitney Canada est à la recherche d’un leader transformationnel pour occuper le poste de Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle. Agissant comme le principal partenaire stratégique du directeur exécutif des technologies numériques, cette personne assurera une maîtrise rigoureuse, une visibilité complète et une exécution disciplinée de l’ensemble du portefeuille de projets numériques de P&WC. Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle traditionnel de suivi de projets, mais d’un poste de leadership stratégique responsable de l’exécution, de la gouvernance, de la santé financière et de l’amélioration continue d’un portefeuille de transformation numérique de plusieurs millions de dollars.

En supervisant des initiatives complexes dans les domaines de l’ingénierie, de la fabrication, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des services après-vente et des fonctions corporatives, le directeur jouera un rôle de liaison essentiel entre P&WC, les organisations de livraison basées en Pologne et le PMO mondial de Pratt & Whitney. En intégrant la responsabilité financière et l’excellence opérationnelle au cadre de gestion du PMO, cette personne veillera à ce que les investissements technologiques stratégiques génèrent une valeur mesurable pour les résultats financiers et une transformation durable de l’entreprise.

Amazon has committed more than $10 billion to Amazon Leo, a low Earth orbit satellite network designed to bring fast, affordable broadband to customers around the world. Production Operations is where that ambition becomes physical. Every Leo satellite weighs more than 1,000 pounds, contains roughly 4 million individual components, and is designed and built in-house on a 172,000 square foot custom production line in Kirkland, Washington, capable of producing up to five satellite a day. The team completed its 1,000th satellite in September 2026 (https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/how-amazon-leo-builds-satellites), making Leo one of the largest and most advanced satellite production operations in the world.  
From the factory, satellites move to a 100,000 square foot payload processing facility at Kennedy Space Center in Florida that can support three launch campaigns at once, and to launch operations in French Guiana. The organization spans eight sites today across multiple states and ground stations across multiple countries, with more investments coming through in the times ahead.  
This role builds on Amazon's deep operations heritage and takes it to newer heights. You will partner with an organization that brings together aerospace, RF, supply chain and manufacturing experts, recruited from the leading space and defense companies, alongside a skilled hourly production and launch workforce building and launching satellite in clean rooms, across shifts, and on mission-critical launch campaigns. Few people leaders anywhere get to shape all of this at once: precision satellite manufacturing across multiple satellite generations, export-controlled and government production, and Amazon Leo's first employing entity outside the US.

You won't be inheriting a playbook. You'll be writing it.  
What makes this role unique  

* Two talent markets, one interwoven strategy.
